doc.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Recording and playing with John
summary: They recorded together on many albums; John's other work and the father and son group.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: Well that’s some great advice, and you guys got to record together a couple of times?

Yeah. He was on all these 13 albums we did with my band. We did a lot of stuff together, two trombones, and we would have done more with that, but you know I think John, and I’ll give him credit, I think he was a little afraid of the dog and pony show idea of the father/son thing. And I don’t fault him for that you know. Because he does these high echelon parties and going on with this group and that group. He was with Harry Connick for a while and was out with Woody and Rich Matteson was a great experience. He went to Japan with Rich and his tuba-euphonium group that he had. And so that’s a good deal. And there are situations where a father and son will form this group and you know six times out of ten the son can’t blow his nose. And it’s sad. Now John, I can go out, we did a thing out in Topeka, Kansas for the jazz society and kicked their butt man, we did it. And still people say wow. But part of our playing together is we both pretty much know

what each other’s going to do and so it comes out so rehearsed sounding when it isn’t sometimes. Now we rehearse stuff, but, so I’m very proud of him. Like I say I’m very sad that my dad never heard me play or him. But I’ve been lucky. It seems like my big career push was kind of based around Disney and that, and as much as I bitch about Disney’s music program pretty much being gutted, I mean it’s pathetic, but I can’t fault Disney. They put me on the map. I’ll never forget that. I mean I came down here and every day I discover something. Oh my God, I’ve only read about this guy and he’s coming to sit in with our band or coming to direct the band, and that Meredith Wilson thing and Rob McConnell was in town. Because Disney had a really active music program with the college students. And you asked — and I got sidetracked — I think music schools are great. I think it’s sad because they’re turning out droves and droves or wonderful players who either go back to school and train other kids, you know. I don’t know what —
